text:
Dubai recorded 10,379 residential sales totaling AED 29.53 billion over the last four weeks, representing a 2.6 percent increase in volume and a 7.3 percent rise in value compared to the previous four-week period. Mortgage registrations were separate from sales, with 4,047 new mortgage entries recorded during the same timeframe. The market continued to be dominated by off-plan transactions, which accounted for 59.6 percent of all sales.

The median residential price per square foot declined by 1.2 percent to AED 1,677, down from AED 1,697 in the prior period. This slight softening in pricing occurred alongside the shift in the off-plan mix, which dropped from 64.7 percent to 59.6 percent. Top performing areas by sales volume included Dubai South with 3,617 transactions and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,281 transactions over the last twelve weeks.

Rental activity remained robust with 93,465 Ejari contracts registered, of which 50.3 percent were renewals. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 70,000. Estimated gross yields varied significantly by location, with Zaabeel First leading at 9.1 percent for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent and Town Square at 7.0 percent.

Investors should monitor Al Yufrah 1, which saw a 37.7 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks, alongside Saih Shuaib 1 at 13.7 percent. Conversely, Palm Deira cooled by 14.1 percent and Liwan by 13.3 percent. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,024 sales in the last 60 days that deviated significantly from comparable medians. These figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
